reviews.review: Reading some reviews on steam and russian playground.ru, i was a bit disappointed about this game. There were mentioned some mistakes of the developers, concerning behaviour and wearings of the Adeptus Astartes. Never the less, i made up my mind to buy Space Marine. And you know... that was perfect, despite of some mistakes. What about its "minuses" - 1) Its russian dubbing is badly done in some phrases of the main character - sometimes it sounds too indifferent. That irritated me a bit. 2) Meltagun in the game is a kind of shotgun which shoots a cloud of gas, though it releases just a stream, that melts a tank - in cooperation mod it can't humiliate a marine within a shot. 3) Yes, there are some appearance mistakes, which contradicts with the Codex. These are minor mistakes, so if you are not acquainted with precise details of Warhammer "lifestyle", the game will be perfect for playing either in the campaign mode or the coop. Well, "the pluses" - 1) The Ultramarines kill dozens of orcs and heretics. What can be better? 2) Good storyline, i can say it is perfect. Good job. You just should play for a better understanding of its plot. 3) A good cooperation mod, where you can find at least one game. It is good for all the rest Warhammer games, where you have to wait your turn for an hour, 'cause there are no players. 4) Despite of some mistakes, which i described in minuses, the reference to the Warhammer back can be seen here, especially if you know it. The main hero reprimands his subject in narrow interpretation of the Codex and that leads to his departure in the inquisitor's ship. That point leads to forgotten II and XI legions of Adeptus Astartes, forgotten and deleted from Imperial archives. The Ultramarines (as known from some books of Warhammer Horus Heresy) became the biggest legion, just as mainly they were those who recruited marines from these two legions. These marines have one distinctive feature - often they act as they want, not looking into the Codex, while "real" Ultramarines can't but follow it in their belief that no one can be more educated in military science than the Imperator and their Robute Guilliman. This fact points out, that the main character is one of these recruited marines. That fact makes the plot clear and answers everything, concerning this matter. My opinion: don't be afraid to play this game.

This piece is quite underrated in my opinion. It's as close as we'll ever get to a warhammer 40k mmorpg and still the game itself lacks a real community of players who regularly play it. Game without community is like a body without soul. It doesn't really matter that it has a pretty badass Terminatus DLC where you play as a chaos marine because there is actually nobody playing it. Still, the single player is worth playing and some game modes are still being played, so you might just be lucky and experience some of the multiplayer stuff as well. The replayability is decent only if you have friends who play it as well.

you dont have to know anything about warhammer 40k to have fun with this game the gameplay mechanics are solid and the multiplayer is alive and kicking play on the weekends for easist time finding lobbys

While waiting for Eternal Crusade you may want to pick up this little item.  40K fans will love it... if you don't have the love for the universe a lot of it will be lost on you.  Will be playing it over and over I am sure hunting achievments.  Looking for some friends to play some Co-op!

Good game, plays well even on a mediocre laptop. The story that drives the game is well written, with some nice twists - enjoyable even if you dont play the tabletop game. 

main drawback is how quickly things become repetitive. The multiplayer aspects are largely the same - shoot, die, respawn with limited character customisation (though there is some through the 'perks' system). If you do enjoy multiplayer I would strongly recomend getting the dreadnought DLC - fighting this thing is very cool (and difficult!) while playing as it makes you feel like a true angel of death!

All round, a very good game.
